name: Motmot Green
lede: Motmot Green is a muted yellowish green named for the motmot, a Central and South American bird with iridescent green-backed plumage, charted by Ridgway in 1912 and confirmed by the ISCC-NBS system in 1955.

sections.title: A bird's back, charted twice
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 color nomenclature lists this tone on plate XVIII, hue 35 prime [1]. The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 revisited it in block 136, "moderate yellowish green", and Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary dates it to the same year, 1912, plate 27 B 10 [1]. No book held in color-kb discusses "Motmot Green" itself [4].

Its nearest distinct named neighbor is [[deep-malachite-green]], 2.6 units off, "almost the same" by our graph [3]. It sits between the brighter [[corsage-green]] and the duller [[grey-green]], both within 5 units [3]. A fourth, lighter cousin in the library is [[verdigris-green]], 4.9 units off and described as "lighter and more vivid" [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Motmot Green is rare in our archive: 38 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.16 percent, as photographed, concentrated almost entirely in the twentieth century [2]. Gustav Klimt's works carry it at 37.6 times the archive's base rate and Auguste Renoir's at 19.6 times, both well above the usual run of painters [2]. Counts are computed matches on varnished, photographed paintings, not pigment identifications [2]. The bird itself, native to Central and South American forests, is named in English after its soft, repeated call [1].
